2607.29527.title: TerraNova: A Foundation Model for the Anthropocene
2607.29527.paper_summary: A defining problem of the Anthropocene is to model the physical Earth and human societies as one coupled system, yet no learned representation spans their observational breadth. We argue the obstacle is geometric: the physical Earth is measured as continuous fields that ignore political borders, whereas societies are reported for administrative units. Earth-system foundation models serve the first geometry; coupling it to the second has required lossy averaging over borders. We introduce TerraNova, a foundation model trained on 1,024 physical and societal records in their native geometries: 512 gridded Earth-system fields and 512 national indicators. Dedicated encoders represent location, country, time and task, cross-modal transformers fuse them into a shared spatiotemporal state, and a hypernetwork generates a per-query decoder whose evidential head returns a predictive distribution. Two contrastive objectives couple the representation: a population-weighted alignment between each country and coordinates in its territory, and one to pretrained geospatial embeddings carrying image-derived semantics. Read out through that decoder, the representation is competitive with purpose-built geospatial encoders while spanning axes they do not represent (time, oceans and uncertainty) and supporting country-level capabilities. The frozen backbone reconstructs dense fields from sparse observations and adapts to unseen variables in minutes on consumer hardware.
2607.29527.paper_summary_zh: 一個定義人類世的問題是將物理地球和人類社會建模為一個耦合系統，但目前沒有任何學術表述能涵蓋它們的觀測範圍。我們認為障礙在於幾何：物理地球被測量為忽略政治邊界的連續場，而社會則是以行政單位報告的。地球系統基礎模型服務於第一種幾何；將其耦合到第二種幾何需要在邊界上進行有損平均。我們介紹TerraNova，一個基於1,024個物理和社會記錄在其原生幾何上訓練的基礎模型：512個網格化的地球系統場和512個國家指標。專用編碼器表示位置、國家、時間和任務，跨模態Transformer將它們融合成一個共享的時空狀態，而超網絡生成每個查詢的解碼器，其證據頭返回預測分佈。兩個對比目標耦合該表示：每個國家與其領土坐標之間的按人口加權對齊，以及一個與預訓練的地理空間嵌入相對應，該嵌入承載圖像衍生的語義。通過該解碼器讀出，該表示在與專門構建的地理空間編碼器競爭的同時，涵蓋了它們未表示的軸（時間、海洋和不確定性），並支持國家級能力。凍結的主幹從稀疏觀測中重建密集場，並在消費者硬體上在幾分鐘內適應未見變數。
2607.29527.author: Carlos Rodriguez-Pardo et.al.
